LESSON: LENGTH

Grade: SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade two
Subject: MATHEMATICAL ACTIVITIES
Strand: MEASUREMENT
Topic 2.1: Length
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 6

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Length, part of MEASUREMENT in SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade two MATHEMATICAL ACTIVITIES.

Key inquiry question: How can you measure different lengths? 2. Why is measurement of length important?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Length together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
● Critical thinking and problem solving: learner makes 1-metre sticks and uses them in measuring length of various

objects.

● Self-efficacy: learner measures the length of different objects at home, records the measurements and discusses with peers

in school.

Values:
• Responsibility: learner uses locally available materials to make 1-metre sticks and use them to measure the length of

various objects.

• Unity: learner works in teams to make 1-metre sticks and use them to measure the length of various objects.

28

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

● Self-esteem: learner measures the length of different objects at home, record the measurements and discuss with peers in

school.

● Creative thinking: learner uses locally available materials to make 1-metre stick.

Link to Other Learning Areas:

● The learner is able to relate the concept of using objects within the classroom and at home for learning to the concept of

resources in the environment in Environmental Activities.

Suggested Learning Resources:

Pencils, 1-m sticks, rulers, strings, rope, sticks of different lengths. Other Objects in the classroom.
